title: Cardinal Billing Account Repeat Lateness in a Term: Training Questions on the Repeat-Lateness Rate
content:
**Rule.** A repeat-lateness rate applies to the late fee charge of a Cardinal Billing Account and multiplies it: **1.40** when two or more late fees have already been charged in the current term, **1.20** when exactly one has, and **1.00** when none has.

## Questions answered

**Which late fees count?**
The late fees already charged on the account in the current policy term, the term the account is currently billing, as shown by the late fee entries for that term on the billing history. The charge being figured is not one of them.

**Do late fees from an earlier term count?**
No. Only late fees of the current term count.

**What rate applies to the first late fee of a term?**
None has already been charged in the term, so the rate is 1.00.

**And to the second and third?**
The second is charged when exactly one has already been charged: 1.20. The third is charged when two have already been charged: 1.40.

| Late fees already charged in the current term | Repeat-lateness rate |
|---|---|
| 0 | 1.00 |
| 1 | 1.20 |
| 2 or more | 1.40 |

**Hypothetical figure.** A charge figured at $15.00 on an installment of a term in which two late fees have already been charged is multiplied by 1.40.
